claims.text: erosive esophagitis 20 mg QD for 4 to 8 wks.
claims.quote: Treatment of EE due to Acid-Mediated GERD | 20 mg once daily | 4 to 8 weeks The efficacy of PRILOSEC used for longer than 8 weeks in patients with EE has not been established. If a patient does not respond to 8 weeks of treatment, an additional 4 weeks of treatment may be given. If there is recurrence of EE or GERD symptoms (e.g., heartburn), additional 4 to 8 week courses of PRILOSEC may be considered.

claims.text: PPIs are contraindicated w rilpivirine-containing prod.
claims.quote: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), including PRILOSEC, are contraindicated in patients receiving rilpivirine-containing products

claims.text: Hypomagnesemia (rare, USU after a yr of therapy) can cause tetany, arrhythmias and seizures;
claims.quote: Hypomagnesemia, symptomatic and asymptomatic, has been reported rarely in patients treated with PPIs for at least three months, in most cases after a year of therapy. Serious adverse events include tetany, arrhythmias, and seizures.

claims.text: consider checking magnesium b4 starting and periodically w prolonged tx, or w digoxin or drugs that can cause hypomagnesemia (eg, diuretics).
claims.quote: For patients expected to be on prolonged treatment or who take PPIs with medications such as digoxin or drugs that may cause hypomagnesemia (e.g., diuretics), health care professionals may consider monitoring magnesium levels prior to initiation of PPI treatment and periodically

claims.text: Omeprazole w MTX (mainly ↑dose) may raise and prolong MTX levels, possibly causing toxicity;
claims.quote: Concomitant use of omeprazole with methotrexate (primarily at high dose) may elevate and prolong serum concentrations of methotrexate and/or its metabolite hydroxymethotrexate, possibly leading to methotrexate toxicities

claims.text: a temp PPI hold may be considered w ↑dose MTX.
claims.quote: A temporary withdrawal of PRILOSEC may be considered in some patients receiving high-dose methotrexate.
